key_insight: A unified analytical model links diagnosis and design for PEC cells by quantifying how optical, transport, recombination, and interfacial losses shape performance in both BIJ and SEJ architectures.
engineering_relevance: The framework turns experimental current-voltage curves into actionable loss budgets and design targets, helping engineers choose materials and interventions that improve solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency.
method: Builds a physically consistent loss model for BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes
Fits measured current-voltage data to decompose thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial losses
Uses efficiency maps and Sankey diagrams to expose limits and guide optimization
evidence_signal: The abstract says the model is validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, and compared across Si, perovskites, hematite, and BiVO4.
watch_item: Because the framework relies on fitting experimental J–V data and idealized assumptions, its guidance may depend strongly on data quality and how well real device physics matches the model.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
